title: Developer Experience: SDK Guides, Quickstarts & Templates, API Examples, Docs Site Operating Procedures, Top Support Issues and Canonical Fixes
author: Priya Sharma
body:
Overview

Purpose: This document consolidates standards, operating procedures, canonical templates and the top support issues for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation across SDK guides, quickstarts, API examples and the docs site. It is intended for technical writers, SDK engineers, DevEx oncall, and product owners who contribute content to Redwood's public and internal docs.

Scope
- SDK guides (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java)
- Quickstarts and templates (getting-started flows, repo templates, sample apps)
- API examples (REST, SDKs, streaming, tool-calling)
- Docs site operating procedures (review/publish workflow, CI checks, release cadence)
- Top support issues and canonical fixes (issue patterns, troubleshooting steps, reproducible repros)

Document structure
1) Standards & conventions
2) Docs site operating procedures
3) SDK guide structure & required content
4) Quickstarts and template catalog + naming conventions
5) API examples and runnable snippets
6) Top support issues and canonical fixes (canonical PRs/patches)
7) Ownership, SLAs and escalation
8) Appendix: snippets, templates and links

1) Standards & conventions
- Tone: concise, developer-first, prioritized for reproducibility. Use complete sentences and explicit commands.
- File naming: kebab-case, end with year when versioned (e.g. python-sdk-quickstart-2026.md).
- Doc metadata required: title, summary (1 sentence), audience, prerequisites, owner, reviewers, last_updated, links.
- Code samples: must be copy-paste runnable. Each sample must include: install step, minimal auth snippet, minimal request, expected response or output.
- Supported SDK versions: list explicitly at top of each SDK guide (e.g., python-sdk v1.7+).

2) Docs site operating procedures
Purpose: keep the public/docs site consistent, secure and low-friction for contributors.

2.1 Publishing workflow (high level)- Author creates a markdown file under the docs repo (docs/).- Open PR targeting main/docs (branch naming: docs/{area}/{short-desc}).- CI checks run: linter, spellcheck, markdown-link-check, sample-runner test suites.- At least one reviewer from DevEx and one from Product must approve.- Merge window: daily for non-breaking content; 48-hour review for API or sample changes that affect SDKs.- Post-merge: staging site auto-deploy (staging.redwood.internal) and smoke tests (sample-runner).- Production deploy: scheduled daily at 02:00 UTC with automated sitemap and cache purge. Urgent hotfixes follow incident process below.

2.2 CI checks (required)
- mkdocs build: no build errors.
- markdown-link-check: 0 broken internal links.
- sample-runner: all runnable snippets must pass with the sandbox token.
- license-check: no unapproved third-party code.
- accessibility-check: basic a11y scan for headings, alt text.

2.3 Review rubric (quick checklist for reviewers)
- Accuracy: commands and endpoints are verified against current API spec.
- Reproducibility: sample-runner reproduces claimed outputs.
- Security: no secret tokens, no customer data.
- UX: flow is understandable for 20-minute completion.

2.4 Hotfix / incident-driven docs updates- Trigger: documentation contributes to an incident (e.g., wrong example caused broken customer flows).- Action: open an urgent docs PR with prefix hotfix/docs, tag @oncall-devex, and include remediation steps.- Approvals: DevEx lead + oncall SRE.- Deploy: manual production deploy with rollback plan.

3) SDK guides (structure & required content)
Every SDK guide must include the following sections in order:
- Title and one-line summary
- Compatibility table (SDK versions, supported runtime versions)
- Prerequisites (API key setup, environment variables, minimal billing config)
- Installation (pip/npm/go install commands)
- Quick example: authenticate + simple completion + error handling
- Advanced patterns: streaming, function/tool-calling, long-running batching examples, retry/backoff config
- Best practices & common pitfalls (tokenization, rate limits, concurrency configs)
- Troubleshooting (map of common errors -> fixes)
- API reference link (auto-generated)

3.1 Example: Python minimal quickstart (must be included in every Python guide)
# Install
# pip install redwood-inference
from redwood import Client
client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))
resp = client.completions.create(model='rw-instruct-2.0', prompt='Translate to French: Hello world')
print(resp.text)

Expected output: "Bonjour le monde" (may vary by model).

4) Quickstarts & templates
Quickstart types:
- Hello-API (2-min): a single-file example showing auth and a completion call.
- Chatbot sample app (15-min): TypeScript + Next.js example demonstrating streaming + tool calls.
- Embeddings pipeline (10-min): minimal batch embedding + vector store integration (FAISS example).
- Private deployment example (onprem-readme): skeleton showing config snippets for VPC and KMS integration.

Template catalog (repo path conventions)
- templates/hello-api-python-2026/
- templates/chatbot-nextjs-typescript-2026/
- templates/embeddings-faiss-python-2026/
- templates/onprem-reference-terraform-2026/

Each template must include:
- README with estimated completion time
- LICENSE and security-notes.md 
- CI workflow (GitHub Actions) that runs linters and sample-runner
- PR template: docs-template-pr.md referencing the review rubric

4.1 Template release process- Major updates to templates must include migration notes.
- Tag template releases with semver and update the template index (docs/templates-index.md).

5) API examples and runnable snippets
Rules for API examples:
- Prefer REST + SDK variants for each example.
- Include both synchronous and streaming variants where applicable.
- For streaming examples, include a small interactive snippet and server-side sample for secure polling.

Common example: function/tool calling (REST + Node SDK)
# REST example (curl)
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-chat-3.0","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Get the latest price of AAPL"}],"tools":[{"name":"stock_price","args":{"symbol":"AAPL"}}]}'

# Expected: chat response that includes tool invocation output or fallback if tool unavailable

5.1 Sample-runner expectations
- All code snippets must be included in the sample-runner test matrix.
- Sample-runner runs against the internal sandbox key and asserts on schema rather than exact text where stochastic outputs are expected.

6) Top support issues and canonical fixes
Summary: These are the five recurring support problems observed Jan 2025\u2013Jan 2026 and the canonical repo fixes or docs updates that resolve them. Include minimal repro and the authoritative fix.

Issue A: Incorrect authentication pattern in quickstarts (missing bearer prefix)
- Symptom: 401s with code example using header 'Api-Key: <token>' instead of 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'.
- Canonical fix: Update all quickstarts to use Authorization header and add linter rule to detect Api-Key header usage.
- Example fix diff: docs fix PR #4521 (link: /pull/4521)
- Remediation steps for support: search-and-replace in docs repo, notify customers who opened tickets in the last 30 days.

Issue B: Streaming examples hang when used behind proxies (chunked encoding not preserved)
- Symptom: Customers see no chunks until connection closed.
- Root cause: intermediary proxies strip Transfer-Encoding: chunked for 1xx/103 responses.
- Canonical fix: Provide a server-sent-events (SSE) fallback sample and update Node/Python SDKs to support buffered streaming with periodic heartbeats.
- Docs change: add SSE example and network troubleshooting checklist.

Issue C: Embeddings batch size causing OOM in small dev machines
- Symptom: local runs crash on 8GB machines.
- Canonical fix: add recommended batch sizes per model and per machine RAM to embeddings quickstart. Include example that auto-batches with memory-aware heuristics.
- Quick fix snippet: set batch_size=16 for rw-embed-2.0 on <=16GB RAM.

Issue D: Function/tool calling examples rely on synchronous tool availability
- Symptom: when tools timeout, chat falls back to unhelpful responses.
- Canonical fix: add example with async tool orchestration (enqueue + webhook) and explicit timeout/retry patterns.
- Support playbook: when customer sees tool_timeouts, recommend enabling webhook fallback and increasing tool timeout to 10s for external APIs.

Issue E: Outdated model names in SDK samples after model deprecations
- Symptom: 400 errors referencing unknown model id.
- Canonical fix: maintain a docs variables file (docs/_data/models.json) referenced by sample-runner; update when deprecations announced. Add CI check: sample-runner fails if samples reference deprecated models.

6.1 Canonical fixes repository mapping (table)
- docs-linter-rules: repo redwood/devex-lint (rule ids: RL-001, RL-002)
- sample-runner: repo redwood/sample-runner (version pinned in docs CI)
- templates: repo redwood/docs-templates (release tags)

7) Ownership, SLAs and escalation
Owners and contacts:
- DevEx docs owner: Priya Sharma (eng) \u2014 primary contact for content decisions.
- DevEx oncall: managed via rotation slack channel #devex-oncall.
- Sample-runner owner: Jordan Kim (eng-infra).

SLA for doc changes affecting customer flows:
- Critical (security/fees/incorrect auth): 24h remediation target, patch-level approval required.
- High (broken example causing customer outage): 72h remediation target.
- Normal editorial changes: 7 days review/merge target.

Escalation path:
1. Open a docs-hotfix PR and ping @devex-oncall.
2. If no response in 2h, escalate to DevEx lead and SRE oncall.
3. If customer impact persists beyond 12h, notify product + support leadership and prepare a customer advisory.

8) Appendix: snippets, templates and links
- Template index: /docs/templates-index.md
- Sample-runner docs: /docs/sample-runner/README.md
- Linter repo: https://github.com/redwood/devex-lint
- Hotfix PR template: docs/.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/hotfix-docs.md

Canonical template for new SDK guide (copy-paste)
Title: {SDK} SDK Guide
Summary: One-line summary
Audience: ML Engineers, Backend Engineers
Prereqs: API key, python 3.10+
Compatibility: {sdk_versions}
Sections:
- Installation
- Quickstart
- Advanced patterns
- Troubleshooting
- Reference links
Owner: @owner-handle
Reviewers: @devex, @product-owner
Last updated: YYYY-MM-DD

Contact & feedback
- For doc content changes: submit PR to docs repo and assign Priya Sharma.
- For CI issues: open an issue in redwood/sample-runner and tag Jordan Kim.
- For urgent support related to docs causing outages: use the incident process in oncall-and-incident-response/incident-process.

Notes
- This playbook is reviewed quarterly. Next scheduled review: 2026-05-01.
